claims.text: In a collection with a self-referencing relation field that has cascadeDelete enabled, deleting a record also deletes its descendants at every nesting level (children, grandchildren and deeper), not only the direct children.
Cascade deletion through a self-referencing relation only removes records that (transitively) reference the deleted record; unrelated records and records in other branches remain.
Deleting a leaf record in a self-referencing hierarchy succeeds and leaves its ancestors intact.
